items.title: Section: Dying Without Fear — The Arhat Bitten by a Poisonous Snake, and Xuánzàng's Own Final, Lucid Days

items.zh: 又於行等都不執著我及我所；由此因緣，色等壞時亦不恐怖。由此相貌，顯彼自體已得清淨。
items.en:
Furthermore, clinging to no self or what belongs to self within any conditioned phenomenon, when form and the rest come apart, this too brings no fear — and this very absence of fear reveals that one's own being has already achieved purity.
From the Great Commentary: the pure practice having been beautifully established, the noble path well cultivated, one greets the exhaustion of the lifespan with joy, exactly as one might set down a container once holding poison.

items.zh: 又由彼識永清淨故，不待餘因，任運自然入於寂滅。此識相續究竟斷故，於十方界不復流轉。

items.title: Section: Six Final Angles — Freedom From Desire, From Feeling's Shadow, and All the Way to Utter Purity

items.zh: 於命及死不希求故，名永離欲。又所有受是識樹影，彼於爾時不復有故，名永離影；諸有漏識，於現法中畢竟滅盡，故名寂滅。諸無漏識，隨其次第，有學解脫，名為寂靜。無學解脫，名曰清涼。餘依永滅，故說清淨。
items.en: Because such a one no longer seeks either life or death, this is called permanent freedom from desire. And because all feeling — the very shadow cast by consciousness's own tree — no longer arises at this point, this is called permanent freedom from shadow. Because every contaminated consciousness has been utterly exhausted within the present, this is called quiescence. Because the uncontaminated consciousness belonging, in sequence, to the learner's own liberation still remains, this is called tranquility. The liberation of one beyond further learning is called coolness. Because the remaining residue is permanently extinguished, this is called purity.

items.zh: 又復諸識自性非染，由世尊說一切心性本清淨故。所以者何？非心自性畢竟不淨能生過失，猶如貪等一切煩惱。亦不獨為煩惱因緣，如色受等。所以者何？以必無有獨於識性而起染愛，如於色等。是故唯識不立識住。是名識蘊由住差別。

items.title: Section: Consciousness's Fifth and Final Distinction — Twenty Kinds of Mind Through Craving, Aversion, and Their Absence

items.zh: 云何異相差別？謂有貪心、離貪心、有瞋心、離瞋心等，如經廣說乃至不解脫心、極解脫心，是名一門異相差別。
items.en: What is the distinction by differing aspects? It is such things as a craving mind, a mind free of craving, an aversive mind, a mind free of aversion, and so on as extensively explained in the scriptures, all the way up to the unliberated mind and the utterly liberated mind — this is called one approach to the distinction by differing aspects.

items.title: Section: Mind Classified by Realm — Four Kinds in the Desire Realm, Three Each Above, and Two Beyond All Three

items.zh: 復有約界異相差別。謂欲界有四心，善心、不善心、有覆無記心、無覆無記心。色界有三心，除不善。無色界有三心，亦除不善。無漏有二心，有學及無學。又欲界善心有二種，謂加行及生得。無覆無記心有四種，異熟生心、威儀路心、工巧處心，及變化心。此唯是生得，謂天、龍、藥叉等。然無修果心。於色界中，無工巧處心，無色界亦爾。當知善心，如下，上亦爾，一切處有。
items.en:
There is also a distinction by realm. The desire realm has four kinds of mind: wholesome, unwholesome, obscured-neutral, and unobscured-neutral. The form realm has three, excluding the unwholesome. The formless realm has three, likewise excluding the unwholesome. The uncontaminated has two, the learner's and the one beyond learning's.
The desire realm's wholesome mind is of two kinds: effortful and innate. The unobscured-neutral mind is of four kinds: karma-ripened, deportment, craft, and transformation. This last is solely innate, as with devas, nāgas, and yakṣas, without any cultivated result. In the form realm there is no craft mind, and likewise in the formless realm. One should know that the wholesome mind, as below so above, exists everywhere.

items.title: Section: Sixteen Minds Classified by What Severs Them — The Four Truths Across Three Realms, Plus the Uncontaminated

items.zh: 又有約種異相差別。謂欲界有五心。一、見苦所斷心，二、見集所斷心，三、見滅所斷心，四、見道所斷心，五、修道所斷心。如欲界有五心，如是色、無色界各有五心。并無漏心，總為十六。
items.en: There is also a distinction by what is severed. The desire realm has five minds: severed through seeing suffering, severed through seeing its origin, severed through seeing its cessation, severed through seeing the path, and severed through the path of cultivation. As the desire realm has these five, so too do the form and formless realms each have five. Adding the uncontaminated mind, the total comes to sixteen.

items.title: Section: Three Grades of Practitioner, and the Very Beginner's Simple Alternation Between Affliction and Its Absence

items.zh: 初異相心差別義，我當分別。一切有情略有三品。一、未發趣定品；二、雖已發趣，未得定品；三、已得定品。此復二種。一、不清淨，二、極清淨。於初品中，或時起染污心，由貪等纏繞彼心故。或時起善、無記心，由貪等纏暫遠離故。
items.en:
I shall now explain the earlier distinction by differing aspects. All beings may be briefly divided into three grades: those who have not yet set out towards meditative concentration; those who have set out towards it but not yet attained it; and those who have already attained it. Each of these is further of two kinds: impure and utterly pure.
Within the first grade, at times a defiled mind arises, bound by craving and the rest. At times a wholesome or neutral mind arises, craving and the rest having been momentarily set at a distance.

items.title: Section: The Second Grade's Eight Minds — Scattering, Sinking, Rousing, Over-Rousing, and Finally Settling Into Quiet

items.zh: 第二品中，或時令心於內靜息。或時失念，於五妙欲其心馳散。或時極靜息故，便為惛沈睡眠纏覆其心。或時為斷彼故，於淨妙境安處其心。或時於彼不正安處，心便掉舉。若正安處，便不掉舉。由沈掉蓋未斷滅故，於彼二品俱不寂靜。由斷滅故，心得寂靜。
items.en: Within the second grade, at times the mind is made to settle quietly inward. At times, losing mindfulness, it runs scattered towards the five sensory pleasures. At times, through excessive quieting, dullness and drowsiness come to envelop the mind. At times, in order to sever this, the mind is placed upon a pure and excellent object. At times, improperly placed there, the mind becomes agitated. When properly placed, it does not become agitated. Because the two hindrances of dullness and agitation remain unsevered, in both respects the mind is not yet settled. Once they are severed, the mind attains settledness.

items.title: Section: The Third Grade's Mind, and the Complete Closing of Consciousness's Five Distinctions

items.zh: 若由如理作意，已得根本靜慮，名定心；若未得者，名不定心。道究竟故，名善修心；斷究竟故，名極解脫心。與此相違，名不善修心及不解脫心。從定心已來，當知是第三品。是名識蘊異相差別。
items.en: Having, through proper reflection, already attained a fundamental meditative absorption, this is called a concentrated mind; not yet having attained it, this is called an unconcentrated mind. The path having reached its own completion, this is called a well-cultivated mind; the severance having reached its own completion, this is called the mind of utmost liberation. The opposite of these are called the poorly cultivated mind and the unliberated mind. From the concentrated mind onward, one should know this belongs to the third grade. This is called consciousness aggregate's distinction by differing aspects.

items.zh: 復次，云何諸蘊次第？謂說差別。此復五種應知。一、生起所作，二、對治所作，三、流轉所作，四、住所作，五、安立所作。

blocks.text: Consciousness at rest, then mind classified many ways, ending with a practical portrait of a meditator swinging between dullness and agitation.
(Untranslated, 0595b28: because consciousness is permanently purified, without needing any other cause it naturally enters stillness, and no longer wanders in the ten directions.)

Feeling is "the shadow of the tree of consciousness". Master Cháng Bǎi: when the six faculties meet their objects in supreme equanimity, the shadow is gone. Tranquillity is the learner's liberation, coolness the arhat's, purity the ending of all residue.

Master Cháng Bǎi: consciousness joined with defiled factors is defiled, with good factors pure. (Untranslated, 0595c06: consciousness is not defiled by nature, "for the Blessed One said that the nature of mind is originally pure"; so consciousness is not itself made a station.)

Four kinds in the desire realm, three each in the higher realms (no unwholesome), and two uncontaminated. Master Cháng Bǎi: the higher realms' afflictions are "obscured-neutral": not strongly bad, but obstructing the noble path.
Five in each realm (four cut by seeing the truths, one by cultivation), plus the uncontaminated mind.

Not yet set out, set out but not attained, and attained. Master Cháng Bǎi: by the worldly path, one counts as pure on attaining fundamental absorption; by the transmundane path, one must cut the afflictions of the three realms.

Excessive quieting brings dullness; to end it, one places the mind on a bright, uplifting object; placed improperly, the mind grows agitated. Master Cháng Bǎi: in dullness one feels as if in absorption, but is not.
When the path is complete, the mind is "well cultivated"; when severance is complete, it is "utterly liberated".
"In dullness one feels as if in absorption." Every meditator meets this. The remedy is not more force but a brighter object.

quiz.q: What is the "shadow" in "permanent freedom from shadow," per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the shadow is the body, mind's shadow, left only at death, so it cannot be gained in life
the shadow is feeling, consciousness's shadow; one abides in supreme equanimity as faculties meet objects, beyond the feelings
the shadow is ignorance, severed only at buddhahood
the shadow is the outer world, an image of mind
quiz.why: The treatise calls feeling the shadow of the tree of consciousness. Master Cháng Bǎi: the shadow means feeling; and with the six faculties meeting the six objects, abiding at all times in supreme equanimity, this state beyond the feelings is permanent freedom from shadow. Ordinary beings, by contrast, make karma under the sway of feelings.

quiz.q: What does the treatise match with tranquility, coolness, and purity?
options: liberation beyond learning is tranquility; the learner's liberation coolness; the ending of contaminated consciousness purity
the ending of contaminated consciousness is tranquility; the learner's liberation coolness; liberation beyond learning purity
all three are names only for an arhat after final nirvāṇa, having nothing to do with the learner's stage
the learner's liberation is tranquility; liberation beyond learning coolness; the permanent ending of the remaining residue purity
quiz.why: The treatise assigns tranquility to the learner's liberation, coolness to liberation beyond learning, and purity to the permanent ending of the residue. Master Cháng Bǎi: the learner's liberation refers to noble ones of the first through third fruits; the arhat, liberated from the afflictions of craving and view of the three realms, is called cool.

quiz.q: The English has "changing aspects" for 異相. According to Master Cháng Bǎi, does 異 mean change here?
options: yes: 異 is the 異 of abiding-with-change, consciousness altering moment by moment, so "changing" is exact and stands
no: 異 means strange, consciousness having magical displays
no: 異 means outsiders' teachings, and should be "heterodox"
no: 異 means differing kinds, consciousness having different aspects through joining pure or defiled factors; "changing" is imprecise
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: consciousness joined with a defiled mind is defiled, and joined with a good mind is pure; from one angle, consciousness joining pure or defiled factors has many differing aspects. So 異相 means differing aspects, sorted by what they are joined with. "Changing" suggests one thing altering over time, which is not the point.

quiz.q: By realm, how many minds does each realm have, and the uncontaminated?
options: the desire realm four; the form and formless realms three each, excluding the unwholesome; the uncontaminated two, of learners and those beyond
the desire realm three; the form and formless realms four each; the uncontaminated two, of learners and those beyond learning
the desire realm four; the form realm three; the formless realm two, without unobscured-neutral; the uncontaminated one
each realm four, the higher realms too having the unwholesome; the uncontaminated two
quiz.why: The treatise gives the desire realm four kinds of mind, the form and formless realms three each without the unwholesome, and the uncontaminated two. Master Cháng Bǎi: the afflictions of the two higher realms are obscured-neutral; though light, they still obstruct attaining the noble path. So absence of the unwholesome there does not mean absence of affliction.

quiz.q: What is the "obscured" of obscured-neutral mind, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: these defiled factors obstruct the noble path, being neither strongly good nor bad, and so count as neutral
覆 is clothing covering the body, for desire-realm beings dress, and so it is neutral
this mind brings strong evil results and is really unwholesome, not neutral, the treatise speaking loosely here
覆 means seeds suppressed by absorption, not manifesting for a while
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 覆 means that these defiled mental factors can obstruct the noble path; they are not strongly good or bad, and so belong to the neutral. Thus "obscured" concerns obstruction of the path, not the quality of the result, which is why such a mind can be neutral and yet be an obstacle.

quiz.q: Why does the desire realm's transformation mind have no cultivated result? What does such a result require?
options: desire-realm beings never practice, and so have no wholesome mind at all
a cultivated result is uncontaminated, found only in arhats, so devas and nāgas cannot have it and the desire realm knows no practice whatever
a cultivated result needs monastic precepts, which householders lack
it is only innate, as with devas, nāgas, and yakṣas; a cultivated result needs absorption, and exists from the form-realm gods upwards
quiz.why: The treatise says the desire realm's transformation mind is solely innate, as with devas, nāgas, and yakṣas, without any cultivated result. Master Cháng Bǎi: a cultivated-result mind belongs only to those from the form-realm gods upwards, to those with absorption. So the marvels of these beings come with birth and not from practice.

quiz.q: How are the sixteen minds of the distinction by what is severed counted?
options: each of the four truths has four minds, four fours making sixteen, with nothing added or left out
the desire realm ten, and each higher realm three, making sixteen
each realm has four minds severed by seeing the truths and one by cultivation, fifteen in all, and with the uncontaminated mind sixteen
fifteen moments of the path of seeing, plus the first of cultivation
quiz.why: The treatise gives each of the three realms five minds, four severed by seeing the truths and one by cultivation, and adding the uncontaminated mind totals sixteen. Master Cháng Bǎi: after the first fruit one enters the path of cultivation and must still sever innate afflictions, and this is the mind severed by cultivation. These minds are what is severed, not what severs.

quiz.q: Into what three grades are all beings briefly divided?
options: śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas, divided by the vehicle towards which they are headed in their practice
those of the desire, form, and formless realms
those not yet set out towards concentration, those set out but not attained, and those who have attained it
those of inferior, middling, and superior restraint
quiz.why: The treatise divides all beings by their relation to concentration: not yet set out, set out but not attained, and attained. Master Cháng Bǎi on the second: desire-realm beings who wish to practise absorption but have not gained it. The three grades serve to explain the earlier list of twenty minds.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish impure and utterly pure?
options: those who have taken precepts are utterly pure and those who have not impure, regardless of concentration
access concentration is already utterly pure, fundamental absorption being a further grade; the transmundane has no bearing on this distinction
desire-realm beings are all impure, and higher beings all utterly pure
by the worldly path, attaining fundamental absorption is utterly pure; by the transmundane, severing craving and view of the three realms; access concentration with afflictions remaining is impure
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: by the worldly path, one counts as utterly pure on attaining fundamental absorption; by the transmundane path, one must sever the afflictions of craving and view of the three realms. Someone who has access concentration, with afflictions not fully severed, still counts as impure.

quiz.q: The English has "placed upon a radiant object" for 淨妙境. How does the lecture describe it, and is "radiant" enough?
options: it is the light seen in absorption, so "radiant" is exactly right; the treatise simply means visualising light and nothing else
it is the five sensual pleasures, and "radiant" should be "sensual"
it is a pure, fine object that gladdens and rouses the mind; "radiant" takes only the sense of light and loses 淨 and 妙
it is signless suchness, and "radiant" should be "signless"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these pure and fine objects gladden and rouse the mind, and so drive off the sunken mind of dullness and drowsiness. What matters is the uplifting quality of the object. "Radiant" catches brightness, one useful aspect against dullness, but it loses "pure" and "fine," and suggests only a visual image.

quiz.q: Why does the mind of the second grade sink at times and grow agitated at times?
options: excessive quieting brings dullness and drowsiness; placing it on a fine object to end these, improper placing brings agitation
excessive quieting brings agitation; placing it on a fine object to end this, improper placing brings dullness and drowsiness
both come from improper diet, unrelated to the method of practice, and improve of themselves once diet is adjusted
both come from past karmic obstruction, which practice cannot change
quiz.why: The treatise describes a swing: excessive quieting brings dullness and drowsiness; to end this one places the mind on a fine object; placed improperly, the mind grows agitated. Master Cháng Bǎi: in dullness one feels as if in absorption but is really dozing; until these two hindrances are severed, neither calm nor insight can settle.

quiz.q: How does the treatise distinguish the well-cultivated mind and the mind of utmost liberation?
options: severance's completion is the well-cultivated mind; the path's completion the mind of utmost liberation
attaining fundamental absorption is the well-cultivated mind; not attaining it the mind of utmost liberation, since there remains room to advance
they are two names for one mind, with no difference
the path's completion is the well-cultivated mind; severance's completion the mind of utmost liberation
quiz.why: The treatise pairs the two: the path having reached completion is the well-cultivated mind, and severance having reached completion is the mind of utmost liberation. Master Cháng Bǎi: when the path of calm and insight is complete, this is the well-cultivated mind; when severing afflictions is complete, the mind of utmost liberation.
